questions.q: An IPv4 address like 192.168.1.10 is made up of how many bits total?
options: 8 bits
16 bits
32 bits
64 bits
questions.explain: An IPv4 address is 32 bits total: four octets of 8 bits each, written in dotted-decimal notation.

questions.q: What do the two parts of an IP address — the network portion and the host portion — identify?
options: The network portion identifies the device's manufacturer; the host portion identifies its model
The network portion identifies which network a device is on; the host portion identifies the specific device within that network
The network portion is for IPv4 only; the host portion is for IPv6 only
They are two names for the same thing
questions.explain: Every IP address splits into a network portion (which network) and a host portion (which specific device on that network), similar to a street name and an apartment number.

questions.q: Why can Northbridge Retail's warehouse LAN safely reuse a private address range like 192.168.10.0/24 without conflicting with the rest of the internet?
options: Private addresses are encrypted so no conflict is possible
Private address ranges are never routed on the public internet, so they only need to be unique inside Northbridge's own network
Private addresses automatically change every day
Every company is assigned a unique private range by a global authority
questions.explain: Private IP ranges (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) are reserved for internal use and are never routed on the public internet, so the same ranges can be reused inside many different private networks.

questions.q: What does NAT (Network Address Translation) do when a device on Northbridge's private warehouse LAN needs to reach the public internet?
options: It deletes the device's IP address entirely
It swaps the device's private source address for a public address so the traffic can be routed on the internet
It converts the IP address into a MAC address
It assigns the device a static address permanently
questions.explain: NAT translates a private internal address into a public, globally routable address so traffic from a private network can reach and return from the internet.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a static and a dynamic IP address assignment?
options: Static addresses are always public; dynamic addresses are always private
A static address is manually configured and never changes, while a dynamic address is automatically assigned (commonly by DHCP) and can change
Dynamic addresses are only used by servers; static addresses are only used by laptops
There is no real difference
questions.explain: Static addressing is a manual, unchanging configuration used for devices that need to be reliably found, while dynamic addressing (typically via DHCP) is assigned automatically from a pool as devices join and leave the network.
